method: Mechanical scan of every HTML, Markdown, JSON, CSV and Python file outside this folder, plus a comparison of the cost files that several sections publish for the same route. No other session's file was modified: the findings are reported, and where a figure affects the price, this section publishes its own verified value.

checks.check: Files scanned (HTML, MD, JSON, CSV, PY)
checks.detail: Everything in the repository except this folder and .git.
Every published page in every section, including superseded ones.
Every href in every HTML page resolved against the file system.
Zero means no page links to a file that does not exist.

checks.check: Pages showing dollar figures with no external source link
checks.detail: of 147 pages. Listed under irregularities where the figures are cost or tax claims.

checks.check: Content sections not linked from the landing page
Distinct FEIE values published across the repo
Distinct HSBC fee-cap values published across the repo
Source ids referenced by this section that exist in the ledger
checks.detail: Checked by verify.py on every build.

irregularities.finding: The same BOC wire at USD 10,000 is published as $53.36 in guide-fb2f2562 and $53.37 here, and at USD 400,000 as $898.54 versus $898.75. estimate-facf2fe9 publishes $55.16 and $967.38 for the same route and amounts.
irregularities.effect: Three prices for one action, differing by up to $68.84 at USD 400,000. The cause is a different reference midpoint and a different board timestamp, not a different fee. This section states its midpoint and board timestamp on the cost page so the number can be reproduced.

irregularities.finding: The guide records the BOC board as buy 666.06 / sell 668.86 and the HSBC board as sell 6.7053746. The boards read for this section on 2026-11-11 20:39 are 665.91 / 668.71 and 6.7030239.
irregularities.effect: Costs computed from the older snapshot are about 0.02% high at BOC. The ranking of routes is unchanged because the gap between the two banks' spreads is far larger than the daily move.

irregularities.finding: 780 dollar figures appear in this page with no external source link anywhere in the document.
irregularities.effect: A reader cannot check any of the numbers from the page itself. The ledger for that section exists elsewhere in the folder but is not linked from the table.

irregularities.finding: The landing page links 20 of the 27 content sections. Not linked: acceptance-373b54a3, acceptance-a64bd476, audit-456e7542, audit-6068a908, verify-88f5a1be.
irregularities.effect: Published work is unreachable from the front door, so a reader cannot tell whether it exists or has been superseded.

irregularities.finding: The foreign earned income exclusion appears as 132,900, 137,300, 126,500, 120,000 and 112,000 in different folders, sometimes without the tax year next to the number.
irregularities.effect: Only 137,300 is the figure for tax years beginning in 2027 [S26]; 132,900 is the 2026 figure. A number without a year cannot be verified, so this section always states the year.

irregularities.finding: The HSBC fee cap is published as CNY 500 in some folders and as CNY 620 in others.
irregularities.effect: Both can be right: 500 is the commission cap and 620 is the commission cap plus the 120 cable charge. Pages that print 620 as a 'cap' without the breakdown invite double counting.

irregularities.finding: Several folders publish their own cost ladder for the same 40 amounts with slightly different formulas and reference midpoints.
irregularities.effect: Redundant arithmetic that drifts apart every time a board is re-read. This section keeps one model (model.py) and one ledger, and the review page names the other versions rather than averaging them.

irregularities.finding: The integration landing page prices BOC at 669.11 (board timestamp 2026-11-11 10:25:02). The board read for this section at 20:39:19 the same day shows 668.71 for the same quote.
irregularities.effect: Two different same-day prices for the same bank and the same product, a 0.06% move within one day. Any cost built on a board rate is only valid for the timestamp printed next to it, which is why every page here states its timestamp.

irregularities.finding: Some pages describe conversion pricing as a 'penalty' without separating it from PRC income tax that is due whether or not the money moves.
irregularities.effect: Readers over-estimate the cost of converting. The penalty page here splits nine layers so the tax on the source income is not counted as a conversion cost.
